title: Sara-Bay Financial Makes Big Bet on MercadoLibre, Adds $12 Million Worth of Stock
content:
What happened

According to its SEC filing dated April 17, 2026, Sara-Bay Financial increased its position in MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) by 6,288 shares during the first quarter. The estimated value of this purchase is $12.13 million, based on the average closing price over the quarter. At quarter-end, the position was valued at $11.18 million, an increase of $10.82 million from the prior filing period, reflecting both additional shares and price movement.

What else to know

Sara-Bay Financial added to its MercadoLibre position, bringing the stake to 3.36% of 13F reportable AUM.

Top holdings after the filing:

Helios Technologies: $74.67 million (22.5% of AUM) Nvidia: $55.55 million (16.7% of AUM) Centrus Energy: $26.72 million (8.0% of AUM) JPMorgan Chase: $17.47 million (5.3% of AUM) Meta Platforms: $16.13 million (4.9% of AUM)

As of April 16, 2026, MercadoLibre shares were trading at $1,822.13, down 10% over the past year and underperforming the S&P 500 by 45 percentage points.

Company overview

Metric Value Price (as of market close 2026-04-16) $1,822.13 Market Capitalization $94.55 billion Revenue (TTM) $28.89 billion Net Income (TTM) $2.00 billion

Company snapshot

MercadoLibre:

Operates the Mercado Libre Marketplace, Mercado Pago fintech platform, Mercado Envios logistics, and additional digital commerce solutions across Latin America. Generates revenue primarily through transaction fees, payment processing, logistics services, advertising, and financial products for merchants and consumers. Serves businesses, merchants, and individual consumers throughout Latin America, with a focus on e-commerce and digital financial services.

MercadoLibre is a leading e-commerce and fintech platform in Latin America, leveraging its integrated marketplace and payment infrastructure to drive growth at scale. The company combines online retail, digital payments, and logistics to create a comprehensive ecosystem for both buyers and sellers. Its broad reach and continuous innovation in financial technology provide a significant competitive advantage in a rapidly expanding digital market.

What this transaction means for investors

I’ve seen several firms adding MercadoLibre shares recently, and I love to see Sara-Bay Financial do the same, since I am a shareholder. Sara-Bay has held numerous positions since 2020, so it typically takes a long-term view, which is nice to see as a Foolish investor. While it made small adds to MELI stock in Q3 and Q4 last year, it ramped up its bet in a major way in Q1, making the company its 9th-largest holding now.

MercadoLibre’s stock remains 29% below its 52-week high, but I’d argue that its operations look as strong as ever, so I’ll also continue to “buy the dip” on this long-term outperformer. Growing sales, unique active buyers, and fintech monthly active users by 45%, 24%, and 27%, respectively, MercadoLibre continues to fire on all cylinders, even though its stock has taken a breather.

Story Continues

Currently trading at 37 times forward earnings, MELI stock looks reasonably priced considering its persistent growth and remaining growth optionality. With e-commerce penetration in Latin America roughly half that of the U.S. and China -- and basic banking services not yet near 100% for the population throughout the region -- MercadoLibre’s growth story is still probably in its early chapters. MELI stock is a 66-bagger since 2007, and Sara-Bay seems to think the good times should return over time -- and I can’t help but agree .

title: A. O. Smith, Winnebago, Gates Industrial Corporation, Helios, and Fortune Brands Stocks Trade Down, What You Need To Know
content:
What Happened?

A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after news of a potential Middle East ceasefire triggered a major shift in the stock market. For weeks, investors held defensive and energy stocks during the conflict between the U.S. and Iran.

With a peace deal being discussed, the risk of global supply chain issues decreased significantly. This caused oil prices to drop sharply, leading many traders to sell their defensive shares to lock in profits while the global situation stabilizes. Instead of holding onto traditional companies, investors rotated back into high-growth technology names.

Tech leaders like Broadcom and Tesla saw gains as the market's "fear index" hit a seven-week low. Analysts believed that a more stable global environment makes high-growth investments much more appealing than defensive industrial ones. Because of this rotation, the industrial sector trailed the rest of the market as buyers searched for bigger returns in the tech sector.

The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

title: Helios Technologies Unveils CORE 2030 at Investor Day: Double Sales, 25%+ EBITDA, M&A Ahead
content:
Key Points

Helios’ CORE 2030 plan targets doubling sales by 2030 and lifting adjusted EBITDA to >25%, driven by a structured Helios Momentum Model and Helios Business System with a mix of organic growth and disciplined M&A. The company reported pro forma 2025 revenue of $792 million (reported $839M) and 19.2% adjusted EBITDA, returned to growth with Q3 +13% and Q4 +17%, and is guiding to at least 20% growth at the low end of 2026 guidance while exiting 2025 with net leverage of 1.8x. Operational and portfolio actions include a >30% dividend increase, a $100 million buyback authorization (≈$14M repurchased), and segment expansion plans—electronics now ~40% of revenue with EMEA/APAC upside and hydraulics pushing into defense/aerospace certifications and data‑center liquid cooling opportunities. Interested in Helios Technologies, Inc? Here are five stocks we like better.

Helios Gets Support Along 50-Day Line Ahead Of November 8 Earnings Report

Helios Technologies (NYSE:HLIO) used its 2026 Investor Day in Sarasota, Florida, to outline a growth and margin expansion plan it calls its CORE 2030 strategy, while also reviewing recent operating progress and a shift toward a more disciplined operating model and capital allocation framework.

Company snapshot and recent turnaround

Vice President of Investor Relations and Corporate Communication Tania Almond said the company recently reported 2025 results of $839 million in revenue, and noted that the company completed a divestiture in 2025. On a pro forma basis excluding that divested business, she said results were $792 million. Almond also said that electronics now represents nearly 40% of total revenue, and that the company’s mix remains diversified by channel and end market.

→ Quiet BNY and Northern Trust Reward Patient Investors

Almond and CEO Sean Bagan described a multi-year period of organic sales declines and margin pressure following a pandemic-era surge in consumer-facing categories such as recreation and wellness. Almond said the company returned to growth in 2025 after 12 consecutive quarters of declines.

CORE 2030: doubling sales and lifting profitability

Bagan said Helios is pursuing a plan to “double the size” of sales by 2030, supported by what the company calls the Helios Momentum Model. He emphasized a more structured operating cadence through the Helios Business System, including strategic planning, goal deployment, quarterly and monthly business reviews, and monthly go-to-market reviews where revenue-generating sales teams report out to leadership.

→ The Silicon Squeeze: AI Pricing Power Lifts Chip Stocks

Story Continues

Bagan highlighted several 2025 proof points tied to the company’s commercial and product execution:

$60 million of new business wins in 2025, described as projected annual run-rate business as programs ramp. 11 “meaningful” product launches in 2025, which management characterized as incremental (not cannibalizing existing products). Employee metrics including 30 “boomerang” employees returning to the company, average tenure of 9 years, and an employee net promoter score increase of 13 points year over year.

Bagan also said the company exited 2025 with improving growth rates, citing 13% sales growth in the third quarter and 17% in the fourth quarter, and noted that the company’s 2026 outlook included at least 20% growth at the low end of the company’s guidance range. He said Helios’ commitment includes reaching adjusted EBITDA margins exceeding 25% over time.

Segment highlights: electronics and hydraulics

→ Meta Reportedly Plans 20% Layoff: A Sign of Weakness or Strength?

Billy Aldridge, president of the electronics segment, described the business as providing rugged hardware, software, and systems-level solutions. He said electronics is heavily weighted to North America (about 80%) and that the segment is “underserved” in EMEA and APAC, which management views as an expansion opportunity.

Aldridge said Balboa Water Group is a market leader in health and wellness, and he referenced a recent press release involving Jacuzzi to add more content. He also said Balboa is launching more product in the current year than in the last 10 years, and highlighted water care initiatives such as PureZone and a broader move toward more intelligent, sensing-driven solutions.

On the hydraulics side, Rick Martich, president of hydraulics for motion control technologies, emphasized brand trust and described Sun Hydraulics’ cartridge valves and manifold-integrated packages as being used in critical load-holding applications. He also highlighted focus areas including defense and aerospace, citing efforts such as pursuing ITAR and CMMC certifications to support deeper penetration.

Matteo Arduini, president of hydraulics for fluid conveyance technologies, described Faster’s coupling and multi-connection portfolio and said agriculture represents about 60% of Faster’s business, with construction and mobile equipment as the second-largest market. Arduini discussed new and adjacent markets including oil and gas, hydrogen applications, and what he called “real news” for Faster: thermal management for data centers. He said Faster developed and tested its own product for data center liquid cooling systems, built a dedicated supply chain, and is under NDA with “important OEMs and hyperscaler” customers, though he said the opportunity is not yet reflected as current sales.

Financial path to 2030: organic growth, M&A, and shareholder returns

CFO Jeremy Evans presented a framework for reaching the 2030 targets, beginning with the pro forma 2025 base of $792 million and citing a 2026 guidance midpoint of $840 million. Evans said the company expects organic revenue to grow to roughly $1.1 billion by 2030, leaving a roughly $500 million gap to be filled through acquisitions.

Evans said the company reported 19.2% adjusted EBITDA in 2025 and targeted 25%+ by 2030, driven by volume, productivity, footprint optimization, and portfolio actions, including the margin benefit from the divestiture of Custom Fluidpower. He said the company expects free cash conversion of about 100% and capex of 3% to 6% of sales, reflecting equipment replacement, product-related investments, and automation.

Evans also discussed capital allocation, noting the company paid down $153 million of debt across 2024 and 2025 and exited 2025 with net leverage of 1.8x, within a target range of 1.5x to 2.5x. He said the company’s dividend track record spans more than 28 years and that the board approved a more than 30% increase in the dividend for the first quarter of 2026—the first dividend increase in company history. Evans also reviewed the company’s $100 million share repurchase authorization and said the company repurchased about $14 million, or roughly 1% of shares, under that program.

On M&A, leadership emphasized greater discipline and integration planning. Evans said targets must meet strategic criteria around culture, product fit, and market growth potential, and financial guardrails including year-one accretion, targeted synergies, and ROIC discipline. He noted that Helios’ 2025 ROIC was 5.7% excluding an impairment charge and said the company is targeting low-to-mid teens ROIC over time.

In closing remarks, Bagan said the company is focused on “consistent, scalable execution” to meet its 2030 commitments, with momentum supported by product development, commercial execution, operational efficiency efforts, and a balance sheet positioned to re-enter acquisitions under a defined framework.

About Helios Technologies (NYSE:HLIO)

Helios Technologies, Inc develops and manufactures engineered motion control and electronic control products for a wide range of industrial and mobile equipment applications. The company's Hydraulics segment designs and produces hydraulic cartridge valves, manifold systems, pumps and motors, filtration solutions and off-highway joysticks. Its Electronic Controls segment offers programmable electronic control units, wireless telematics, human-machine interfaces and software to optimize performance, efficiency and safety for equipment OEMs and end users.

Through its global network of manufacturing facilities, service centers and technology centers, Helios Technologies serves markets in agriculture, construction, material handling, mining, municipal and recreational vehicles, as well as industrial automation and infrastructure equipment.

title: Helios Stock: Emerging Growth Catalysts and the Key Risks in 2026
content:
Helios Technologies, Inc. HLIO is leaning into a growth playbook that depends less on a macro bounce and more on what it can generate internally. The company is increasing the pace of new product launches, a stronger go-to-market motion, and a broader commercial funnel to fund growth with its own wins.

That approach can work well in cyclical industries, where demand improves in waves and investors reward companies that keep building share through the cycle. The opportunity is tangible. The risk is timing and execution, especially as 2026 progresses.

The New-Products Engine Is the Core Story

The central catalyst for 2026 is Helios’ claim that growth is increasingly self-funded through a strengthened go-to-market model and an elevated launch cadence. The company booked more than $50 million of new commercial wins in 2025, with ramps expected to continue through 2026. Just as important, the sales funnel expanded substantially. In motion control, this is often where the market re-rates a story. Companies like Parker-Hannifin Corporation PH and Eaton Corporation plc ETN tend to be rewarded when new products and commercial execution show up in mix and margin, not just in revenue. Helios is trying to put itself in that lane.

How Cross-Sell Could Lift Share of Wallet

Helios’ 2026 priorities are clear. The company is focused on converting the funnel into wins and expanding cross-sell to deepen share of wallet. It also plans to keep new product launches increasing, reinforcing the idea that innovation is not a one-time push but an ongoing operating rhythm.

Health & Wellness market is a targeted effort inside that framework. The company refreshed its portfolio in Health & Wellness market with the goal of outgrowing what is described as a low-growth category. That makes this initiative less about riding market demand and more about taking share through product and channel execution.

The near-term signal investors should look for is a steady pace of wins that show up across customers and geographies. Cross-sell works best when it is repeatable, not occasional.

Helios Technologies, Inc Price and Consensus

Helios Technologies, Inc price-consensus-chart | Helios Technologies, Inc Quote

Electronics Could Outgrow Hydraulics in 2026

Within the segment outlook, Helios expects Electronics segment to outpace Hydraulics segment in 2026. At midpoints, the expectation is Electronics will be up 7% while Hydraulics is anticipated to be up 5%. That is a notable shift in mix, given how investors typically view electronics-heavy growth profiles.

Electronics unit delivered strong momentum exiting 2025, but the gains were concentrated among selective original equipment manufacturer (OEM) customers. In the fourth quarter of 2025, one large recreational OEM drove most of the improvement.

Story Continues

New Adjacencies Add Optionality

Helios is also pointing to new adjacencies that can expand optionality over time. Aerospace market is called out as one such adjacency, and the strategic value is straightforward: it adds another vector for growth that is not purely tied to the same industrial cycles as the core portfolio.

This is a long-term opportunity. It complements the near-term cyclical recovery rather than replacing it. The near-term story still hinges on funnel conversion and product ramps. But adjacencies can help sustain growth when core markets normalize.

HLIO currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Automation Spend as a Margin and Growth Lever

Helios plans to step up capital spending in 2026 from 2025’s level of about 3% of sales. The goal is to back productivity and automation, along with internal capabilities that support product launches.

This matters because it ties growth and margin together. Better internal capabilities can shorten cycle times, improve throughput, and reduce friction during product ramps. That can support operating leverage when volumes improve.

The tradeoff is near-term spend discipline. Higher investment can help the engine run faster, but it also raises the need for clean execution, especially if the second half of 2026 slows as expected.

Tariff Costs Are the Swing Factors

Tariffs remained a headwind in 2025, and tariff costs are expected to be higher year over year in the first quarter of 2026 due to prior ramp timing. While that impact may normalize, broader tariff uncertainty persists.

What Could Break the Bull Case in 2H26?

The core risk framing for 2026 is a strong start and a weaker finish. Tougher comparisons and expected second-half deceleration could shift sentiment, particularly if investors begin to question how much incremental operating leverage is left later in the year.

Execution dependencies are the practical pressure points. Delays in customer approvals, slower distributor sell-through, or product launch timing can push revenue into later periods.

The company is focused on converting its expanded pipeline into diversified wins, reducing reliance on a single large OEM in the Electronics segment, and maintaining margins despite tariff fluctuations.

What the Target Implies

With a 6 –12 month price target of $73 and a current price of $63.83, the implied upside is about 14%. That potential return is tied to an improving near-term demand picture and ongoing margin rebuilding.

The near-term demand case rests on industrial indicators, and a stronger order backdrop that supported 10 straight months of year-over-year order growth through 2025. That trend provides better visibility into the first quarter of 2026 than the company had earlier in the cycle.

On the margin side, the company exited 2025 with a higher gross margin run rate and management actions aimed at operating leverage. If volumes rebuild as expected in the first half of 2026, the target framework assumes incremental profitability can follow.

Those signals align with a setup where the primary debate is less about direction and more about execution pace.

The Style Scores point to the same tension. The VGM Score is B, with Growth at A, Value at D, and Momentum at C. In practice, the market is paying up for a recovery that still needs to be delivered through sustained order conversion, product execution, and continued margin progress.

Earnings Setup After a Strong Q4 Beat

The recent narrative improved materially after a stronger fourth quarter of 2025. Adjusted earnings were 81 cents per share, ahead of the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 71 cents. Revenues were $210.7 million compared with the consensus estimate of $198 million.

Sales increased 17% year over year to $210.7 million. Performance was supported by volume recovery across both segments, a favorable mix and continued productivity actions.

That mix matters for 2026. The fourth-quarter print did not rely on a single lever. It combined demand improvement with operational execution, which is typically the kind of backdrop that sustains confidence into the next year.

Guidance and the Near-Term Headwind List

For 2026, Helios expects revenues of $820-$860 million. The company projects an adjusted EBITDA margin of 19.5-21% and non-GAAP earnings per share of $2.60-$2.90.

Management expects stronger growth in the first half of 2026, which is consistent with the order momentum that improved through 2025. The company also laid out near-term headwinds that investors should not ignore.

Those headwinds include higher tariff costs, potential semiconductor supply constraints and pricing pressures. The key is whether execution and mix can offset those pressures enough to keep the margin rebuild intact.

Valuation vs. Industry and Its Own History

HLIO trades at about 22.30x forward 12-month earnings per share. That compares with 21.87x for the Zacks sub-industry, 21.12x for the Zacks sector, and 21.24x for the S&P 500. In other words, the stock is modestly premium to all three benchmarks.

Over the past five years, the stock has traded as high as 27.46x and as low as 11.14x, with a median of 17.16x. The current multiple sits above that median, suggesting the market is already discounting a meaningful improvement in fundamentals.Zacks Investment Research

That does not make the valuation unworkable, but it raises the stakes. Investors buying here are paying for continued progress, not just stabilization. In the broader motion control and electrification landscape, companies like Parker-Hannifin Corporation PH and Eaton Corporation plc ETN also benefit from infrastructure-linked demand, which can keep investor attention on execution and margin durability across the group.

Capital Allocation Adds a Second Support Pillar

Capital allocation supports the investment case alongside operating improvement. Free cash flow reached a record high in 2025, net leverage declined to 1.8x net debt to adjusted EBITDA exiting 2025, and available liquidity surpassed total debt.

The company has also maintained shareholder returns. It paid its 116th consecutive quarterly dividend and repurchased 330,000 shares for $13.6 million during 2025.

Strong cash generation and reduced leverage provide flexibility. The company has room to keep investing in automation and new products while still supporting dividends and opportunistic repurchases.

The Decision Framework

A practical way to approach HLIO at today’s price is to track a short checklist through the first half of 2026.

It is worth watching for continued order-to-revenue conversion that validates the visibility implied by the 2025 order trend and supports the stronger first-half growth expectation.

Investors should also look for Electronics wins to broaden beyond one large original equipment manufacturer, so growth is not overly concentrated. Its also worth monitoring whether margin progress continues despite higher tariffs and cost pressure, keeping profitability within the guided range.

Investors will also want that the expected deceleration in the second half of 2026 remains manageable and does not materially reduce incremental operating leverage. If those items hold, HLIO can justify its premium multiple and keep the path open toward the target.
